chose: A mutation job runs behind the runner's fence, one savepoint per attempt that only the runner can name: a refused network call or an app error rolls the job back to it, and the worker marks the job failed in the claim's own transaction; code behind an undone fence stays refused and writes nothing more
over: Marking a refused job failed in a transaction of its own (d-4a0e0d02), which left the job pending between its claim's rollback and the mark, so another slot or copy ran it a second time under load
Fencing only this copy's own slots with an in-process set of failing jobs, which leaves the race between copies open
because: A failed job must never run twice; the fence's savepoint is unguessable and taken before the handler, so a handler can't launder writes through it, and the claim's row lock holds until the failure commits
binding: none: this session owns no active work order
